As is the case with all public transit operations in the U.S. today, the NFTA uses operating subsidies to maintain reasonable fare levels for the people it serves. In the future, if operating costs continue to escalate without compensating increases in fare-box revenues, the NFTA may have to increase fares, reduce less productive service, or further utilize operating subsidies such as are presently available from the Federal Government, New York State, and Erie and Niagara Counties.
The figures in Table 4-2 assume possible extensions of the rail transit system to Amherst or Tonawanda do not take place until after 1995. Similar analyses examining the impact of the Amherst Extension from the northern terminus of the proposed rail transit system to the SUNYAB's North Campus show that the projected system deficit would be reduced substantially after the extension is placed in operation.
Construction Schedule
The Metrorail design is divided into three phases: Phase 1 - General Architecture/Engineering and Conceptual Design; Phase 2 - General Architecture/ Engineering and Definitive Design; and Phase 3 - Final Design and construction.
Design work in Phase 2 cannot commence until the EIS is circulated and approved. Final design and construction (Phase 3) must await UMTA's approval of another capital assistance request, which also is dependent upon acceptance of this EIS and other conditions.
Construction is generally divided into four basic types of contracts:
. Structural Contracts--This includes the construction of at-grade sections of the line, cut-and-cover and tunnel subway sections, and station shells. Other activities include utilities' maintenance and relocation, drainage, traffic control, street restoration and underpinning, and floating slab structures to minimize operational noise and vibration.
. Finish Contracts--This includes the finishing work of principal at-grade structures, i.e., architectural finishing of floors, walls, and ceilings; paving and landscaping; electrical and mechanical systems, lighting, service power, water supply, plumbing, and fire protection.
. Combined Contracts—Contracts for selected work which combine the structural and finish elements of construction indicated above.
